analysis.evidence: וַתֹּאמֶר agrees with the feminine singular subject הָאִשָּׁה. The phrase אֶל הַנָּחָשׁ identifies the serpent as her addressee, and נֹאכֵל (“we may eat”) is part of her quoted speech.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person feminine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַתֹּאמֶר הָאִשָּׁה אֶל הַנָּחָשׁ, “the woman said to the serpent,” הָאִשָּׁה identifies the speaker. The feminine singular verb וַתֹּאמֶר agrees with its subject, and the clause expresses no kinship or marital relationship.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun.

draft.change: Add Gen.9.8 as evidence for the existing addressee sense of אֶל at word index 0.
draft.definition: With a verb of speaking, אֶל introduces the addressee.
draft.evidence: In Gen.9.8, וְאֶל בָּנָיו adds Noah’s sons to the hearers already introduced by אֶל נֹחַ.

analysis.evidence: In וַתֹּאמֶר הָאִשָּׁה אֶל הַנָּחָשׁ (“the woman said to the serpent”), אֶל introduces the serpent as the addressee.
analysis.sense: Marks the person or people addressed.

analysis.evidence: וַתֹּאמֶר הָאִשָּׁה אֶל הַנָּחָשׁ means “the woman said to the serpent.” The definite article identifies the serpent that addressed her in the preceding verse.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with prefixed definite article הַ.

analysis.evidence: In מִפְּרִי עֵץ הַגָּן, עֵץ הַגָּן identifies the tree that bears the fruit. The woman says נֹאכֵל, “we may eat,” and מִן marks the fruit of which they may eat.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed partitive מִן, appearing as מִ־ with the nun assimilated into פ.

analysis.evidence: In מִפְּרִי עֵץ הַגָּן, עֵץ stands in construct with הַגָּן, “the garden.” The woman says they eat the fruit of the garden’s trees, so the singular עֵץ refers generically to a living tree.
In מִפְּרִי עֵץ הַגָּן, “from the fruit of the trees of the garden,” הַגָּן completes the construct chain and identifies where the trees grow.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ + common noun, singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: מִפְּרִי עֵץ הַגָּן identifies what may be eaten, the fruit of the garden’s trees. In her reply to the serpent, the woman uses the first-person plural נֹאכֵל to state what they are permitted to eat.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, first person common plural, with preformative נ־ and no suffix.
